## Description

A barrel-shaped hunter (~110 × 80 µm) that strikes paramecia with its proboscis, paralyses them with
toxicysts and swallows them whole, even though they are larger than itself: the cytostome dilates
almost to the body width. Starved, it encysts.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 2 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A raptorial hunter with [toxicysts](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md) (prey touched is paralysed and
dies even if released) and a `mouth_width` of ~70 µm (it swallows a *P. caudatum* ~50 µm wide).
Barrel shape with almost truncated ends. Encysts when prey runs out.

## Literature

- Gause G.F. (1934) *The Struggle for Existence*, fig. 32 (*D. nasutum* with *P. caudatum*; data in
  gauseR): +0.93/day with abundant prey (temperature not verified).
- Wessenberg H., Antipa G. (1970) J. Protozool. 17: 250 (toxicysts; paralysis duration estimated).
- Beers C.D. (1927) (encystment when prey is gone).

## Not implemented yet

- Predator–prey oscillations with immigration are not yet validated (roadmap B).
- Prey capture is not a pexicyst-and-toxicyst two-stage attachment.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Validated in Gause's [predator without refuge](../../mechanics/well-mixed-culture.md); shares toxicysts with
*Dileptus* and *Litonotus* and [cysts](../../mechanics/life-cycle-and-division.md) with many ciliates.
